newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr takes breather in Tokyo after topside capped.
newsitem.headline: Dlr takes breather in Tokyo after topside capped.

text.p: 0315 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar took a breather against the yen by Tokyo midday on Wednesday after failing to break convincingly above 119.50/60 yen, but the underlying trend of the dollar remained bullish, dealers said.
The dollar was caught in tight ranges by late morning as profit-taking and light sales by exporters blocked its upside, while short-covering by interbank operators provided support.

"The dollar's advance was limited around 119.50 yen, but we also confirmed today that there was strong buying interest on dips," a Japanese city bank dealer said. "The dollar is clearly bullish and likely to test 120 yen soon."

The dollar was blocked around 119.50 yen by sales to prevent option orders placed above that level being hit. Japanese exporters also sold sporadically on rallies ahead of a Japanese summer vacation period starting next week.
Along with interbank operators, U.S. securities firms were also detected buying in early trade, sending the greenback as high as 119.59 yen, dealers said.
The mark maintained its strength against the yen on bids by Japanese trust banks, providing support to the dollar/yen.
At 0330 GMT, the mark stood at 63.56/62 yen, compared with 63.45 yen in New York on Tuesday.
The technical trend of the dollar vs the yen improved further, especially after a break through 119 yen overnight, but the market needs fresh incentives to drive up the dollar.

Dealers said they would watch out for remarks by Haruhiko Kuroda, the recently appointed director-general of the Japanese Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, at a meeting of the the Forex Club on Wednesday.
He is expected to speak at the beginning of the meeting, which is scheduled to start around 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).

The market was also concerned about Japan's growing trade surplus, but dealers shrugged off data on the customs-cleared trade surplus for the first 20 days of July announced on Wednesday morning. The Finance Ministry said the surplus rose 126.4 percent to 480.57 billion yen in the period compared with a revised surplus of 212.26 billion yen in the same period last year.
The figure compared with a trade surplus of 453.20 billion yen in the first 20 days of June.
"The market's focus may be temporarily shifting out of the trade issue, and the focus is more on economic fundamentals now," another Japanese bank dealer said.

"The market is becoming more cautious about recent fragility in the Japanese stock market and falling Japanese market rates," the second dealer said. "Operators overseas could use these factors as yen-selling factors to drive up the dollar/yen."
The dollar closed at 119.20/30 yen and 1.8790/800 in New York on Tuesday. ---Chikafumi Hodo, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
